pr_comments: @ferrariofilippo can you look this over? I want to get it merged before #10117. This requires some stress testing, try to break it 🙂

I tried everything I thought of, and it seems the only bug is the one we already know.

I think the user should be able to decide even among grid layout sizes.
At the moment this feature uses the last size selected by the user when `ForceOnAllDirectories` is enabled.
If you want to reproduce:
- Reset preferences
- Enable `ForceOnAllDirectories`
- Set grid layout size
- Disable `ForceOnAllDirectories`
- Change `DefaultLayout` to `Grid`

I think this should be changed because a user would need to do all the above only to change the default items' size for the grid layout.

There are a range of sizes for the grid layouts, perhaps we can support a couple presets in the drop down (small, medium, large). I'm not sure how to do that right now as we don't have enums for those.

> we can support a couple presets in the drop down (small, medium, large)

I think that's enough.
Merged this as is so that we can merge the default column options, should be okay if we add the options later on.

Yes, after all it's working with no bugs.
Choosing the size of `GridView` is a feature we can add later

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
I like to view my files in medium or large icons, but it's defaulted at list view. 

**Describe the solution you'd like**
To have an option to default the view for _all_ folders would be great. I only recently found out that the legacy File Explorer has such an option (Set folders to preferred size, then go to view > options > view > apply to folders > apply/okay). If there were an option in the settings that's more straightforward ("layout mode: [large/medium/small/tiles/details]") that would be awesome!

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Not sure of any other potential alternatives.

**Additional context**
N/A

| Capability | Priority |
| :---------- | :------- |
| This proposal will add a combo box to the folder preferences section allowing users to select the default layout mode | Must |

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/39923744/189020124-07d5c41f-82c4-42f9-b02c-d9d0f95fc2e0.png)
comments:
Thanks for this suggestion. You should already be able to set a default layout by:
- turning off "enable individual preferences for folders" option in Files settings
- setting your desired layout mode for any directory
- turning back on "enable individual preferences for folders"

But it's not really straight forward. (Plus this may not work anymore the latest version)

> Thanks for this suggestion. You should already be able to set a default layout by:
> 
> * turning off "enable individual preferences for folders" option in Files settings
> * setting your desired layout mode for any directory
> * turning back on "enable individual preferences for folders"

> But it's not really straight forward. (Plus this may not work anymore the latest version)

AH THANK YOU!

Thanks. This solved my issue. Really sorry for opening an issue on this but I really couldn't find a way to do it.

I think the option "enable individual preferences for folders" is kinda vague about its functionality. I suggest changing it to make it more clear, like **"Use one layout in all folders"**, **"Use the same layout in all folders"** or something on that sort.

> Thanks. This solved my issue. Really sorry for opening an issue on this but I really couldn't find a way to do it.
> 
> I think the option "enable individual preferences for folders" is kinda vague about its functionality. I suggest changing it to make it more clear, like **"Use one layout in all folders"**, **"Use the same layout in all folders"** or something on that sort.

This is more of a workaround as this setting affects other preferences beyond the layout mode.

> Thanks for this suggestion. You should already be able to set a default layout by:

FYI, this does not work anymore + I cannot even save a layout to a single folder...

EDIT:
Actually, I was able to save the layout of a single folder by setting On "enable individual preferences for folders" and restarting the App. But setting back the option to Off resets everything and nothing is saved.

Thanks that worked for me, but I must say... the way of disabling and re-enabling is not very intuitive... Maybe you can find a more user friendly way of achieving the same goal! Cheers, and thank you for the great tool you provide to us!!!

review_comments: Note that this prevents adaptive layout mode from working because folderSettings.LayoutMode is never set to Adaptive.  Even in adaptive mode folderSettings.LayoutMode is still either details or grid or tiles. The above check for IsAdaptiveLayoutEnabled is what we want.
